item.title: DPS July Updates!!
item.description:
Summer Updates!!

The Division of Design and Construction (DODC) is releasing the following updates:

  • New Design Manual – This document compiles all current design memos, policies, and standards managed by DODC into a single, easy-to-reference document. It includes an annual update process and a live index to identify any standards revised between official releases.
  • New Design Memo: 3.11 – Abandonment of Shoring in the Right-of-Way – This design memo outlines the approval process for private development sites requesting permission to abandon shoring in the Right-of-Way.
  • Updated DPS Standard Construction Drawing: SCD 2319 Curb Ramps – The standard has been revised to clarify that the maximum slope of long flares is measured relative to true horizontal—not the slope of the adjacent street. This update follows direction from ODOT.
  • Updated Sample Plan Title Sheets for CIP and Private Development (Commercial and Subdivision) – DPS will no longer include dates on standard drawings listed on the title sheet, unless a specific past version is required. The CMS title sheet note has been updated to reflect that standard drawings should be the most current available at the time of plan signature, unless otherwise noted.

item.title: DPS Roundabout Design Memo Released
item.description:
DPS Roundabout Design Memo Released

 

As part of our ongoing commitment to safety, sustainability, and operational consistency, the Department of Public Service is pleased to announce the release of

Design Memo 7.04: Modern Roundabout Design

This Design Memo guidance formalizes the City’s position that roundabouts, where feasible, are the preferred intersection control solution, due to their proven benefits in reducing serious crashes, calming traffic, and improving circulation.

Highlights include:

  • Design criteria for mini, single-lane, and multi-lane roundabouts

  • Standards for truck accommodations and bicycle/pedestrian safety

  • Geometry and performance check methodologies for efficient planning and approval

This design guidance is intended to complement all other published design guidance for roundabouts. This design guidance is not intended to cover every facet of roundabout design. Designers should continue to consult the existing publications on roundabout design in addition to this design guidance.

We encourage all consultants, contractors, designers, and City Departments to review and apply the guidance to applicable intersection and roadway projects. Contact your City of Columbus Project Manager with any questions as to how this Design Memo applies to your project.

Thanks!

Department of Public Service, Design & Construction Team

New and Updated DPS Design Memos

To: All City-Approved Consultants, Developers, and Other Agencies

The City of Columbus recently published seven (7) new Design Memos and updated two (2) existing Design Memos as described below. These are effective from the publication date of January 1, 2025. All stakeholders—including consultants, developers, and other agencies—are advised to thoroughly review these new and updated Design Memos:

  • 3.01 - Functional Classification
  • 4.03 - Design Speed
  • 4.04 - References to ODOT L&D
  • 4.11 - Sight Triangles (Updated)
  • 4.13 - Roadway Cross-slopes
  • 5.02 - Cross Section Design
  • 6.31 - Bus Facilities
  • 7.05 - Intersecting Roadways
  • 9.04 - Turning Radii (Updated)

 

Please contact your City of Columbus, DPS Project Manager with any questions or further clarification.

 

The updated documents are available electronically and accessible from the Department of Public Service website and accessed via the links above.

DPS Design Memos

Thanks,

DPS Design Team

The City of Columbus, Department of Public Service, has recently switched over to GovDelivery for all forthcoming update announcements. These updates will include Standard Construction Drawings (SCDs), TSDM, General Design Requirements,  ADA Information, CAD Standards, etc.
